conviction_note: The one thing that decides this print is whether the 2026 EBITDA guide of EUR 60-75m gets raised. H1 alone delivered EUR 42.7m (71% of the low end), H2 2025 delivered EUR 33.9m on a cost base that has since fallen 10.9%, and the margin guide of 22-26.5% sits far below the 31.6% H1 margin, so a raise or an upper-end statement is the base case. That case is partly public, though: Warburg called the targets conservative on 11 Aug. The 2025 raise at 9M moved the stock only +1.5% and then -1.1%, and since H1 the stock has lost 14% on ECB/Fed hikes that also threaten the AUM line. So p_up is 59, not higher, and the scaled +0.99 sits below the +1.8 findings sum because the reaction history and the rate backdrop pull the sign toward 50, not the size.

Warburg (Philipp Kaiser): operating result clearly above expectations, annual targets conservative, H1 EBITDA already 71% of the target (dpa-AFX)
Related-party purchase of a further 2.3% of OSCAR Germany (Dawonia) from majority owner First Capital Partner for EUR 50.5m + EUR 11.8m earn-out
No ad-hoc / Prognoseanpassung filed since the H1 release; latest EQS items are voting-rights notices (20 and 23 Oct) and the Lidl portfolio media release (20 Oct)

new_in_release.expect: EBITDA guide 60-75m and margin guide 22-26.5% raised or narrowed to the upper end (likely, up). AUM guide 55-60bn at risk of being narrowed toward the low end on valuations, FX and slow transactions (down risk), the same shape as Nov 2025.
Q3 EBITDA roughly EUR 15-20m (Q3 2025 15.5m, Q2 2026 19.0m), so 9M of about EUR 58-63m, already at or near the bottom of the full-year range. Up versus the pro-rata bar.
Q3 fundraising and transactions: Q3 market data (CBRE -4% y/y Europe, Savills core markets -8%) suggest flat-to-soft volumes. Mildly down.
Available liquidity (EUR 122.2m at H1) lower after the EUR 50.5m Dawonia stake purchase. Known, but it is the line a seller can point at.

findings.finding: The arithmetic of the company's own numbers puts FY2026 EBITDA at or above the top of the EUR 60-75m guide: H1 delivered EUR 42.7m (Q1 23.7m, Q2 19.0m), the prior year's H2 delivered EUR 33.9m (9M25 44.6m, FY25 63.0m) on a cost base that has since fallen 10.9%, and the margin guide of 22-26.5% sits far below the 31.6% H1 margin. A raise or upper-end narrowing at 9M is the base case, as the 9M 2025 raise was.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 11 Nov 2025 EBITDA guide raise (intraday ad-hoc, AUM guide cut at the same time): +1.53% that day, -1.10% the next. 12 May 2026 strong Q1, guide confirmed: +3.15%. 11 Aug 2026 strong H1, guide confirmed: +3.11%, then -14% over the following three months. 10 Dec 2025 Dawonia carry ad-hoc: +10.93%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Warburg's 'conservative' comment was public on 11 Aug and the stock rose 3.1% then. Since then it has fallen 14% (7.62 to 6.53) against an SDAX down about 4%, and it sits 40% under the lowest broker target (EUR 9.50). If the market were holding a raised EBITDA number, a 14% de-rating on rate news alone would be hard to explain for a fee business whose recurring fees exceed opex. The price trades as if the rate shock threatens the guide; the company-level numbers say it does not.
findings.independence: 9M 2025 precedent of a raise at exactly this report: https://www.eqs-news.com/news/corporate/patrizia-delivers-solid-9m-2025-financial-results-and-specifies-full-year-guidance-for-ebitda-and-aum/274820ec-5f42-47be-83a9-8f46a436d97f_en ; sell-side view that the targets are conservative: https://live.deutsche-boerse.com/nachrichten/ROUNDUP-Patrizia-steigert-Gewinn-kraeftig---Aktie-legt-zu-945a3ae8-940c-42f2-af39-431c66cd46c0

findings.finding: The rate backdrop has turned against real assets in Q3. ECB and Fed hikes on oil-driven inflation hold back buyers (dpa-AFX on Vonovia, 29 Oct 2026, where Vonovia now expects only a broadly stable 2026 valuation). European Q3 investment volume fell 4% y/y (CBRE), the core UK/DE/FR markets fell 8% (Savills), and German commercial volume fell 10% over 9M with no Q3 pickup (Colliers). That points to soft transactions and fundraising, and to risk to the AUM guide (EUR 55.9bn at H1 against a 55-60bn range).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov 2025: the AUM guide was cut beside an EBITDA raise and the stock gave back its first-day gain the next session (-1.10%).
findings.original_quote: Nach vier aufeinanderfolgenden Halbjahresperioden mit Bewertungsgewinnen erwartet das Unternehmen für das Gesamtjahr 2026 ... eine weitgehend stabile Portfoliobewertung (translation: after four consecutive half-years of valuation gains, the company expects a broadly stable portfolio valuation for full-year 2026)
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It is the most likely cause of the 14% de-rating since August. What is left is the transmission to PATRIZIA's AUM line, which only the release can show. Transaction fees are small (EUR 3.8m in H1), so the EBITDA effect is limited. This is a macro-to-company hypothesis.

findings.finding: On 30 Sep 2026 PATRIZIA paid its 58.9% owner First Capital Partner (Wolfgang Egger) EUR 50.5m, plus a possible EUR 11.8m earn-out, for a further 2.3% of the Dawonia holding vehicle. That is about 40% of the EUR 122.2m H1 available liquidity, so the 9M balance sheet will show a visibly lower liquidity line from a related-party deal.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 30 Sep 2026 announcement came at 17:08, after the close. Next session (1 Oct) -0.44%, then +1.63%: no visible reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: The deal is public and drew no reaction. What is new is only how the release presents liquidity and net equity after it. The money buys a larger stake in the flagship fund that pays the Dawonia carry (about EUR 49m gross a year from 2026, per the Dec 2025 ad-hoc) and raises co-investment dividends, so it is not distress. Hence the small size.

findings.finding: First Capital Partner (Egger) holds a standing order to buy up to 3.5m PATRIZIA shares (3.8% of 92.35m) between 3 Jun 2026 and 30 Jun 2027, excluding closed periods. The pre-results closed period ends with publication, so the controlling holder's bid can return on 10 Nov, inside the amc window, in a stock trading about 45k shares a day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The order has been live since June and the stock still fell from about 7.6 to 6.5, so the bid has not stopped declines. It acts as a floor, not a driver.
findings.why_not_priced: The order is public. The timing effect, a buyer absent during the closed period and back on the first post-results session, is not something a thin, 41% free-float tape prices ahead. It is small because the order has demonstrably not set the price.

findings.finding: Q4 business wins announced since H1 support the AUM and fundraising narrative the release will carry: the EUR 4bn food-retail platform expanded with a pan-European Lidl portfolio (20 Oct), a commitment to mobilise GBP 1bn for UK essential housing (9 Oct), and a strategic partnership with Abu Dhabi's ADPIC on infrastructure (9 Oct).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 9 Oct 2026 (ADPIC and UK housing): +1.19%, then -3.53% the next session. 20 Oct (Lidl): +1.90%.
findings.why_not_priced: The items are public. The release may quantify them as Q4 equity raised or AUM, which is what would be new. Small.

outside_window.finding: Dawonia exit-carry payments of about EUR 49m gross a year from 2026 to 2029 (Dec 2025 ad-hoc). Whether an H2 2026 tranche lands, and when, decides FY2026 EBITDA well beyond this print. Only partly addressable at 9M.

baseline_tension: The lean (+0.20, essentially the 20-day run-up of -3.97%) has no positioning content. The findings lean mildly up against a stock that has de-rated 14% since H1, so they cut against the 60-day run-up (-12.7%) rather than agreeing with it. The rate backdrop that caused that de-rating is the main thing that could make a raised guide go unrewarded.
language_note: The German dpa-AFX roundup carried Warburg's read that the annual targets are conservative and that H1 already covers 71% of the target; the English EQS releases and English aggregators did not carry this sell-side framing.

The German dpa-AFX Vonovia piece (29 Oct 2026) carried the ECB/Fed hike context and Vonovia's 'weitgehend stabile Portfoliobewertung' outlook, the domestic read-through for real-asset valuations; English searches returned only the pan-European CBRE/Savills volume series.
The primary company documents (EQS releases, pre-notices, ad-hocs, the related-party release) are bilingual and were read in English; the German versions add nothing.
lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide' (guidance change median 9.0% vs 2.3% reiterated): abs_move_pct raised from 4.5 to 5.5, weighted by about a 60% chance of a guide change, and the guidance finding raised from +1.5 to +2.0 on the guidance scale.

'Let the reaction history move p_up, not abs_move_pct': the name's muted 2025 raise reaction (+1.5/-1.1) now moves p_up only; p_up 58 to 59, a lean on a company-level number held down by partial pricing and the rate backdrop.

'Cash can outweigh a raised guide': re-checked the liquidity line after the EUR 50.5m related-party Dawonia purchase. Kept as a small separate negative (-0.2), because the money buys a carry-paying co-investment and not a cash hole.
'Session check: open with the verdict and only with a timestamp': session_check opens 'amc' with the three 2026 release timestamps and flags the 2025 intraday ad-hoc precedent.
